page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance provisioned on KVM hypervisors. It features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz, backed by 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The instance provides 128 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Hardware flags include AVX-512 foundation instructions, AES cryptography, and FMA extension support. It includes no bundled local NVMe storage and relies on network-attached block storage, while network connectivity operates at a 3 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

The instance exhibits lower single-threaded performance alongside balanced multi-threaded compute capabilities. Synthetic CPU testing yields a single-core stress-ng metric of 1109.99 and a Geekbench single-core score of 933.0, placing single-threaded throughput in lower tier brackets. Multi-threaded benchmark workloads perform predictably in average tiers, registering a stress-ng multi-core result of 11774.7 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5755.0. Large block memory read throughput reaches 76.43 GB/sec, while write operations reach 55.34 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 11.3 million Redis SET operations per second and static web serving speeds of 7.83 GB/sec.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the ecs.se1.4xlarge lies in its lower single-core IPC capabilities and modest baseline networking speeds, balanced against a generous 128 GB memory footprint. Because single-thread compression tasks show performance limitations, workloads requiring maximum single-thread responsiveness may experience bottlenecks. However, the hardware profile delivers adequate multi-core density and memory capacity for memory-intensive applications that do not require localized ephemeral disks. Suitable workloads include medium-scale in-memory key-value databases, caching layers like Redis, general web serving, software compilation tasks, and small-scale LLM text generation.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz, supported by 128 GB of RAM and KVM virtualization. The architecture presents an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, AVX-512 instruction support, baseline 3 Gbps network bandwidth, and no local ephemeral storage. Benchmark results demonstrate average multi-core processing throughput, highlighted by a multi-core Geekbench score of 5755.0 and 11.3 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-core processing exhibits lower performance metrics, with a single-core Geekbench score of 933.0 and reduced single-threaded gzip compression rates. The resource allocation prioritizes high RAM density relative to compute core counts, making this instance efficient for memory-bound applications, Redis caching, static web serving, intermediate database operations, and multi-threaded software compilation pipelines where local disk storage is provided via network storage interfaces.
